{{Use mdy dates|date=April 2021}}

'''Hermine Agavni Kalustyan''' ({{langx|hy|Հերմինէ Աղաւնի Գալուստեան}}, 1914 – 3 September 1989) was a [[Turkish people|Turkish]]-[[Armenians|Armenian]] mathematician, educator, and politician.

== Early life and education ==
Kalustyan was born in 1914 in [[Istanbul]], Turkey. She graduated from Paris High School Teacher Training School and from Istanbul University Mathematics Department. From 1932 to 1936, she was at Ecole Normale Superieure to study math. In 1941, she became the first woman in Turkey to obtain a Ph.D. degree in mathematics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Eden |first1=Alp |last2=Irzik |first2=Gürol |date=2011 |title=German mathematicians in exile in Turkey: Richard von Mises, William Prager, Hilda Geiringer, and their impact on Turkish mathematics|journal=Historia Mathematica|language=en |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=432–459|doi=10.1016/j.hm.2012.07.002|doi-access=free }}</ref> She wrote her dissertation titled "Conformal depiction and the movement of an object" in the [[Istanbul University]] under [[Richard von Mises]] and [[William Prager]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=148656}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kadıoğlu |first1=Sevtap |last2=Şahinbaş Erginöz |first2=Gaye |date=2011 |title=An Emigrant Scientist in Istanbul University: Richard Martin Edler von Mises (1883-1953) |url=https://www.brepolsonline.net/doi/10.1484/J.ALMA.4.1006 |journal=Almagest |language=en |volume=2 |issue=2 |pages=102–123 |doi=10.1484/J.ALMA.4.1006 |issn=1792-2593|url-access=subscription }}</ref> 

== Career ==
Between 1948 and 1973, Kalustyan was appointed principal at Esayan Armenian High School. She also taught mathematics at the Getronagan and Galatasaray lyceums in Istanbul, Turkey.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://bantuhd.blogspot.com/2014/10/hermine-kalustyan-1914-1989.html | title=Hermine Kalustyan (1914-1989)}}</ref> In 1961, she became the republic's first non-Muslim minority woman to serve in parliament<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://armedia.am/eng/news/25829/51-years-later-armenians-return-to-the-turkish-parliament.html | title=51 Years Later Armenians Return to the Turkish Parliament| date=February 11, 2023}}</ref> with her appointment to the transitional parliament (1960–1961) that constructed the [[Turkish Constitution of 1961|1961 Constitution]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lse.ac.uk/europeanInstitute/research/LSEE/PDFs/PhD%20Symposium/Papers%202010/Culhaoglu.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=November 9, 2018 |archive-date=November 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109153134/http://www.lse.ac.uk/europeanInstitute/research/LSEE/PDFs/PhD%20Symposium/Papers%202010/Culhaoglu.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> Afterwards, she became a member of the CHP on February 18, 1961.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ulu |first=Cafer |date=2022-01-04 |title=Armenians in Turkish politics and parliament (1923-1946) |url=https://journalsglobal.com/index.php/jgeb/article/view/116 |journal=Journal of Global Economics and Business |language=en |volume=3 |issue=9 |pages=111–126 |doi=10.31039/jgeb.v3i9.116 |issn=2735-9352|doi-access=free }}</ref> In 1975, she published an Armenian book titled, "Towards the Past and Now: Towards Fezaya", and also moved to France.

==Select publications==

* Ali Çakırbaş (June 2017), Non-Muslim MPs and Their Activities in the Republican Era (1923-1964), Nevşehir: Nevşehir Hacı Bektaş Veli University Social Sciences Institute, p.&nbsp;293, archived from the original on 12 May 2021, access date: 12 May 2021, PhD Thesis
* Nihal Esen (2016), Non-Muslim Members of Parliament in the Republican Era, Elazığ: Fırat University Social Sciences Institute, p.&nbsp;47, archived from the original on 12 May 2021, access date: 12 May 2021, Master's Thesis
* Grand National Assembly of Turkey Album 1920-2010, Volume 4 (1960-1983), p.&nbsp;1641, archived from the original on 21 January 2016, access date: 12 May 2021
